bridge: Builds on C02 arrays and M02 graphs/proofs. Trace by hand first; Python may be used for the bounded implementation.
teaching:
An algorithm specifies steps; a data structure determines how information is organised for those steps. A list scan can inspect every item, while a sorted array permits binary search. Faster lookup can require more costly updates or stronger assumptions, so complexity belongs to a particular operation and representation.

A recursive function solves a problem by calling itself on smaller instances. It needs a base case and a measure that decreases toward it. Each call has its own local state. Draw calls and returns separately: a recursive definition does not execute every line at once.

Big-O describes an asymptotic upper bound, not an exact runtime. Linear search uses at most n comparisons; repeatedly halving a sorted search interval needs on the order of log2(n). Constants, allocation and cache effects still matter in real measurements. First prove that the algorithm returns the correct result under its input assumptions; an incorrect fast result is not an optimisation.
explanation: This lower-bound search returns the first insertion position whose value is at least target, not a boolean membership result. hi is exclusive and can equal len(items). The sorted-input assumption preserves the invariant that a valid insertion position remains inside the interval. Test membership by checking the returned index is in bounds and its value equals target.
exercise: Trace the exact function for targets 0,5,6,9 and input [1,3,5,7], plus an empty list. Record every interval and final insertion index.
solution: Indices are0,2,3,4; empty returns 0. The interval shrinks on every iteration. Searching unsorted input invalidates the reasoning even if one target happens to work.
challenge: Implement recursive sum_list(items,index=0) with an empty-suffix base case. Trace [2,4,6], count additions and explain time and call-stack growth. State an input size limitation of recursion in Python.
challenge_solution: Base index==len returns 0; returns unwind 6,10,12. There are n additions and O(n) stack depth. Python has a recursion limit, so an iterative approach is preferable for large lists. Show termination by increasing index toward the list length.
